item.title: Peoria Co-Responder Unit: How's it fairing after more than a year?
item.description: The Peoria Police Department and Carle Health's Trillium Place have partnered to create a co-responder unit that has responded to over 250 calls and served over 130 clients in its first year, providing mental health support and resources to those in need.

item.title: Former deputy in Sonya Massey killing serving prison sentence, but state officials won’t say where
item.description: Former Sangamon County Sheriff's Deputy Sean Grayson has begun serving his 20-year prison sentence for the murder of Sonya Massey, an unarmed Black woman, in an undisclosed location due to safety and security concerns.

item.title: Officer and civilian employee honored for outstanding work in Normal
item.description: Detective Nicole Bruno and Sarah Vitzthum have been recognized by the Normal Police Department for their outstanding service and commitment to wellness, engagement, professionalism, and integrity.

item.title: Good Samaritan saves driver from flaming vehicle
item.description: A Good Samaritan safely removed an unresponsive driver from a burning vehicle after a crash, saving the driver's life.

item.title: U.S. Ambulances for Ukraine to donate 10 ambulances four-years after invasion started
item.description: US Ambulances for Ukraine is donating 10 ambulances to aid Ukrainian first responders on the 4-year anniversary of the Russian invasion, with donations coming from private providers and fire departments across the US.

item.title: Peoria's first Mister Juneteenth aims to inspire youth
item.description: Diarr Muse, Peoria's first Mister Juneteenth, is working to shape the lives of the youth in a positive way and applications for the 2026 pageant are now open.

item.title: Neighborhood House hosting seminar to help first-time homebuyers in Peoria
item.description: Neighborhood House is hosting a free seminar for first-time homebuyers as part of the Reclaim Peoria Project, which aims to purchase, renovate, and sell salvageable homes to first-time buyers.

item.title: Doctors say multiple respiratory viruses circulating across Central Illinois
item.description: Doctors in Central Illinois are seeing an increase in respiratory illnesses, with influenza A and B, seasonal coronavirus strains, rhinovirus, enterovirus and RSV among the most common viruses, and are recommending frequent handwashing, vaccinations and mask-wearing to prevent the spread.

item.title: Rent more than doubled for businesses at Twin Towers Mall
item.description: Business owners in the Twin Towers Mall main floor have been given five days to accept rent prices increased by thousands of dollars or leave the building, causing panic and concern among the small businesses.

item.title: How tariffs affect the price of board games
item.description: Red Raccoon Games in Bloomington, Illinois has seen price increases of 10-15% on board and card games due to fluctuating tariffs, causing CEO Jamie Mathy to call for more stability for local businesses.
